4.1.2.title: Verra Mobility Employees
4.1.2.text:
All Verra Mobility Employees are required to:

• Comply with this Procedure and related instructions
• Use provided controls and equipment
• Report hazardous manual tasks, incidents, or control failures, and
• Not attempting to lift or move items that are known or suspected to be too heavy or
awkward.

5.1.title: Manual Handling Aids
5.1.text:
Where practicable, equipment must be provided to reduce manual handling risks, including:

• Trolleys or mechanical lifting aids
• Adjustable workstations, and
• Storage systems, designed to minimise bending, reaching, or twisting.

6.3.title: Monitoring and Reviewing Controls Procedure
6.3.text:
The effectiveness of controls must be monitored and reviewed through:

• Workplace inspections
• Incident and hazard reports
• Incident investigations, and
• Employee feedback, and audits.

6.1.title: Hazard Identification, Risk Assessment and Control Procedure
6.1.text:
Hazardous manual tasks must be identified and managed in consultation with employees
and in accordance with the Risk Management Procedure (IMS.03.00.PRO.01).

Where required, a risk assessment must be completed to:

• Better understand the nature and level of risk, and
• Identify appropriate controls to eliminate or minimise the risk.

4.1.title: Specific Roles and Responsibilities Related to this Procedure
4.1.text:
4.1.1. Leaders
Leaders are responsible for:
• Identifying hazardous manual tasks within their area of responsibility
• Ensuring hazardous manual tasks are assessed and controlled
• Consulting with employees when identifying hazards and determining controls as per
Consultation and Communication Management Procedure (IMS.05.01.PRO.01), and
• Ensuring controls are implemented and maintained
4.1.2. Verra Mobility Employees
All Verra Mobility Employees are required to:

• Comply with this Procedure and related instructions
• Use provided controls and equipment
• Report hazardous manual tasks, incidents, or control failures, and
• Not attempting to lift or move items that are known or suspected to be too heavy or
awkward.

6.2.title: Implementing Controls Procedure
6.2.text:
Controls must be selected using the Hierarchy of Control, with a preference for elimination.
Where elimination is not reasonably practicable, controls may include:

• Redesigning tasks to avoid manual handling
• Using mechanical aids or lifting equipment
• Reducing load size or weight
• Storing items at waist height
• Limiting duration or frequency of hazardous manual tasks, and
• Rotating tasks where appropriate.

Employees must not attempt to lift or move items that are known or suspected to be too
heavy or awkward and must report such hazards to their Leader.
